Specificially, the implemented inference pipeline uses the following architecture:

Agent Simulation → Feature Extraction → DeepSet(64) → FlowMatching → Posterior

) maps the 54-dimensional feature vector (reshaped to a 1-element set) to a 64-dimensional summary representation. The DeepSet architecture is used (instead of an MLP) to comply with BayesFlow’s internal architecture requirements for condition passing. With a single set element it is functionally an MLP encoder of the feature vector and should be read as such.

children.value: . The slope is that of the regression of posterior means on true values; a slope below 1 indicates shrinkage toward the prior mean. RMSE / prior SD compares the estimation error with the error of reporting the prior mean. Contraction is one minus the ratio of posterior to prior variance.

Five of the six parameters achieve recovery correlations of 0.92 or higher. Parameter recovery of this kind is the standard check that a model’s parameters can be estimated from data of the available size (

children.value: ) is the least well recovered parameter. Its target behaviour (oddball attribution) is governed by few informative events per session (see

), and its recovery is lowest at low precision weighting (0.64 in the lowest third of the prior range), where participants are not found; in the range of precision weighting occupied by participants it is 0.86.

The correlation between the estimate of one parameter and the true value of another does not exceed 0.21 in absolute value. Within posteriors, noise reactivity and belief momentum are negatively correlated (mean −0.64), so that for a single participant the two are not determined independently of each other.
